paragraphs: Friend, this one is heavy, so let me say it plain. David was supposed to be out at the war with his army, but he stayed home (2 Samuel 11:1). One look from the roof turned into a messenger, then a sleepless night, then a cover-up. A small step into sin doesn't stay small, and every step after it costs more than the last.

Now watch what David does when the cover-up isn't working. He tries one plan, then another, and when Uriah won't cooperate, he writes a letter that ends Uriah's life (2 Samuel 11:15). Uriah was the one man in the story who kept doing right, even when he had every excuse not to (2 Samuel 11:11). Sin hides best behind a busy schedule and a good-sounding message like 'Do not let this matter upset you' (2 Samuel 11:25), and I think that's the danger, friend, because from the outside it can all look handled.

But the last line is the one to carry out of here: 'But the thing that David had done was evil in the sight of the LORD.' (2 Samuel 11:27). David could hide it from the army, from Joab's messenger and from the whole city, but he couldn't hide it from the LORD. That's a hard word, and it's also an honest one, because the LORD sees what we do and calls it what it is. So don't wait for a roof moment to decide who you'll be. Stay close to the Word now, and keep your ovens ready, because this story isn't over.
